question: How big is FedNow now, and how fast is it growing?
answer: FedNow settled 4,997,811 payments worth $274.664 billion in the second quarter of 2026 (54,921 a day), up from 2.7 million payments worth $271.3 billion in the first quarter. There were more than 1,800 live institutions by mid-July 2026 (about 1,600 in January), and the largest payment allowed rose from $500,000 at the July 20, 2023 launch to $1 million in March 2025 and $10 million in November 2025. The library holds only these two quarters of volume, so it cannot show a longer growth trend yet.

items.title: FedNow launches
items.text: The Federal Reserve launched the FedNow Service for instant interbank clearing and settlement, operating continuously on a 24-hour, 365-day basis.
kv: Federal Reserve Financial Services; Reserve Banks

items.title: FedNow Transaction Limit Raised Tenfold, to $10 Million
items.sub: September 5, 2025 · Federal Reserve Financial Services · Press Release
items.text: The instant-payment rail's cap jumps from $1 million to $10 million (effective November 12). With the average payment already past $100,000, FedNow stops being a retail toy and becomes a wholesale-adjacent rail.

items.title: Treasury Turns On FedNow for Federal Disbursements (Digital Payout)
items.text: The Fiscal Service enables FedNow for federal agency payouts — eight-plus agencies live, FEMA pushing disaster money instantly instead of mailing checks. The state itself now pays citizens over the Fed's instant rail: Treasury and Fed plumbing fused at the retail edge, the completion of the EO 14247 arc.

items.title: Regulation J — FedNow Cross-Border via Intermediaries
items.text: Amends subpart C of Regulation J to let FedNow participants use non-Reserve-Bank intermediaries (e.g., correspondent banks) to send funds transfers — explicitly to support private-sector cross-border payment solutions, with FedNow handling the U.S. domestic leg. The instant-payment rail reaching for the border.

items.title: FedNow at Three — the Fed Lays ISO 20022 Track Toward Cross-Border, and Sits Down With the Private Clearing House
items.sub: July 9, 2026 · Federal Reserve Financial Services · Announcement
items.text: Chief FedNow Executive Nick Stanescu's three-year Q&A names four things coming to the Fed's own instant rail: FedACH payee-name verification exposed to FedNow users by API; enhanced ISO 20022 message formats 'that will lay the groundwork for the FedNow Service to enable cross-border payments'; a request-for-payment pilot; and Federal Reserve Financial Services co-chairing a newly established X9 Fraud Forum jointly with The Clearing House. Read the last one twice. The Clearing House is the private rail owned by the biggest banks — RTP, the thing FedNow was built to compete with — and the Fed is now its co-chair on a shared standards body. The public rail and the incumbents' rail write the fraud rulebook together. Same absorption grammar as Cede & Co. surviving the DTC rewrite and Visa/Mastercard keeping their own book.

items.title: FedNow's Third Birthday — 1,800 Banks, $271B a Quarter, and a Ceiling Raised Twentyfold
items.sub: July 15, 2026 · Federal Reserve Financial Services · Report
items.text: Fed360's anniversary item puts numbers on the public rail: 1,800+ live institutions, up from about 1,600 in January; seven of the ten largest U.S. banks aboard; Q1 2026 volume 2.7 million transactions worth $271.3 billion; reach claimed at over half of all American checking and savings accounts. The line worth keeping is the ceiling: launched at $500,000, lifted to $1 million in March 2025, lifted again to $10 million in November 2025. A retail instant-payments service does not need a ten-million-dollar transaction limit. That is a wholesale rail wearing a consumer coat.
kv: $500,000 at launch; $1 million from March 2025; $10 million from November 2025

research.title: Fed Payment Stack Control Finality And Clock Gap
research.answer: There is no single payments stack but five control layers on different clocks. Findings: the clock gap (clearing, guarantee and token hours extend faster than securities-transfer and central-bank cash hours, so private prefunded liquidity bridges the gap)…

research.title: The Fed is many legal bodies, and its building cost doubled
research.answer: The Federal Reserve remains a congressionally created system of Board, FOMC and separately chartered Reserve Banks—not a literal fourth branch—but 2026 doctrine preserves exceptional cause protection for Governors.
